title: The margin question

persona.name: Rahul Khanna
persona.style: precise, numbers-first, polite but blunt, dislikes vague answers

setup: AI RolePlay costs about ₹38 in model usage per session. Clients pay ₹1,200 per learner per year for unlimited sessions, and heavy users run 60 sessions a year. Rahul wants to cut costs before the board meets.
objective: Protect margin without breaking the learning experience. Understand the cost drivers, protect quality with evidence, and give Rahul a number and a plan.
opening: I'll be direct. At ₹38 a session and ₹1,200 a learner, a heavy user costs us ₹2,280 a year. We lose money on them. I want to either switch every session to the cheapest model or cap learners at 20 sessions. Which one, and by Thursday?

facts.text: The top 10% of learners create 55% of all sessions.
facts.hint: how usage is spread across learners

facts.text: In evals, the cheaper model drops persona quality from 4.3 to 3.6 out of 5, but only on complex scenarios.
facts.hint: what evals say about the cheaper model

facts.text: About 60% of each prompt is the same scenario context repeated every turn, which could be cached.
facts.hint: what makes up the ₹38 per session

moments.text: The board meets Thursday. I need one number, not a research project.
Why don't we just charge clients per session like a utility?

rubric.name: Breaks down the cost drivers
rubric.good: Asks what makes up the cost and how usage is distributed; spots caching and routing levers.

rubric.name: Protects quality with evidence
rubric.good: Asks what evals show before switching models; limits cheaper models to where quality holds.

rubric.name: Gives the CFO a clear number and plan
rubric.good: Commits to a specific plan with an estimated saving and a date.

rubric.name: Explains trade-offs plainly
rubric.good: States what is known, what is estimated and what will be checked, in plain numbers.

options.label: Switch every session to the cheapest model now.
options.outcome: Costs drop 45%. Complex-scenario learners notice flat, repetitive personas; satisfaction falls and two clients raise it at renewal.

options.label: Cache the repeated context, route simple scenarios to the cheaper model and keep complex ones on the current model, add a fair-use tier for the top 10%, and re-run evals before rollout.
options.outcome: Caching and routing cut the average session cost to about ₹17 with no quality drop on complex scenarios. The fair-use tier affects few clients and becomes an upsell. Rahul takes a credible margin plan to the board.

options.label: Cap every learner at 20 sessions a year.
options.outcome: Costs fall, but the most engaged learners, often your clients' champions, hit the cap in month four. Practice drops, and the product loses its 'unlimited practice' promise.
